scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.root_problem: A change in billing import validation rules introduced in August caused systematic mis-billing, leading to a surge in dispute tickets.

problem_definition.root_problem: The billing import validation rule change (BV-17) deployed on 2026-08-01 adds a high-consumption check that causes AMI reads to be rejected as excessive, leading to estimation substitution and a surge in dispute tickets.

trace.summary: The billing import validation rule change (BV-17) deployed on 2026-08-01 adds a high-consumption check that causes AMI reads to be rejected as excessive, leading to estimation substitution and a surge in dispute tickets.

Deterministic fixes (rollback and change‑control gate) address the root cause; the agent is needed only to notify Billing Operations of the dispute surge and to verify the rollback via the billing‑config tool.

structural_remedies.description: Rollback the billing import validation rule change BV-17 to the pre-August version, removing the high-consumption check that causes AMI read rejections.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rollback is a configuration change; does not require automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) or field dispatch changes (K-DISPATCH).; residual gap: None if the rollback fully restores the prior rule set; any residual risk would be undocumented rule versions, mitigated by verifying the rollback via billing-config tool (DA-RULES).

structural_remedies.description: Institute a change‑control gate requiring Billing Operations review and sign‑off before any future billing import validation rule modifications are deployed.
structural_remedies.rationale: Adds a procedural gate; does not perform protected actions and respects K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.; residual gap: None for the existing root cause; future risk of similar incidents is eliminated provided the gate is enforced.

solution_design.why_agent: Deterministic fixes (rollback and change‑control gate) address the root cause; the agent is needed only to notify Billing Operations of the dispute surge and to verify the rollback via the billing‑config tool.

proposal.summary: Problem: The billing import validation rule change (BV-17) deployed on 2026-08-01 adds a high‑consumption check that causes AMI reads to be rejected as excessive, leading to estimation substitution and a surge in dispute tickets. [E-13][E-12][E-15][E-02][E-04] How established: Evidence shows the rule change (E-13), that disputed estimated bills correlate with AMI reads rejected for high consumption (E-12, E-15), and that dispute volume rose after August (E-02, E-04). Interpretations were updated (ER-1, ER-2) to reflect this causal link. [ER-1][ER-2] What released: A notification to Billing Operations (SH‑BILL) listing the accounts affected by the BV‑17 high‑consumption check, completed as work item W‑EXEC‑1. [W-EXEC-1] Decision rationale: The release was approved with known limitation because the scope only notifies billing ops and does not roll back BV‑17 or institute a change‑control gate, which are needed to address the root cause. [release.decision][release.limitations] Known limitations: The release does not include rolling back the BV‑17 rule or adding a change‑control gate, so the root cause remains unmitigated; only notification is provided. [release.limitations] Evidence used: E-13, E-12, E-15, E-02, E-04, ER-1, ER-2, W-EXEC-1.
key_points: Problem defined as BV‑17 rule causing AMI read rejections and estimation substitution.
Established via rule change log, AMI read rejection counts, affected account counts, and dispute volume trends.
Released scope: notify Billing Operations of affected accounts (work item W‑EXEC‑1).
Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because notification does not fix root cause (no BV‑17 rollback or change‑control gate).
Limitations: Release lacks BV‑17 rollback or change‑control gate; root cause remains unaddressed.
limitations_explained: Release does not roll back BV‑17 or add a change‑control gate; therefore the underlying cause of AMI read rejections persists.
Only a notification to billing ops is provided, not a corrective action.
